channel.title: Southern Legends
channel.description: Profiles of the people still building in Northeast Alabama. From Anniston to Jacksonville to Heflin — makers, farmers, monument stewards, and small business owners who kept going. Hosted by Matt Headley.

item.title: The Hospital
item.description: I left the ER with a spring in my step. The next day, I called Dad to take me back. An essay about a psychiatric hospitalization, the people who drove me there, and what I found on the other side.

item.title: The Burning Bus
item.description: On Mother's Day 1961, a mob firebombed a Greyhound bus full of Freedom Riders outside Anniston. The Freedom Riders National Monument preserves both sites where it happened — and forces a city to reckon with the hardest chapter in its history.

item.title: The Digital Gym
item.description: The Sunday after my first sermon in twelve months, I pulled over on the side of the road — not because something was wrong with the car, but because the comments were coming in too fast to ignore. Then Wade called. I'm calling it the Digital Gym.
